paper_metadata.title: OUTCOME OF EXTRATEMPORAL EPILEPSY SURGERY EXPERIENCE OF A SINGLE CENTER

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study describes a consecutive cohort of 218 adult patients from a single specialized center with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and detailed baseline characteristics. While it is a single-center study, the recruitment process is transparent and representative of the target population of surgical candidates.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: We retrospectively studied the operative outcome in 218 consecutive adult patients with extratemporal lesions who underwent resective surgical treatment for intractable partial epilepsy in the Bethel Epilepsy Center, Bielefeld, Germany, between 1991 and 2005.
items.reasoning: The population is clearly defined as adult patients with intractable extratemporal epilepsy at a specific clinical center.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We retrospectively reviewed the records of all adult patients (16 yr of age) who underwent epilepsy surgery at the Bethel Epilepsy Center, Bielefeld, Germany, from 1991 to 2005. There were 243 consecutive patients.
items.reasoning: The study uses a consecutive sampling method from medical records, which minimizes selection bias within that center.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between 1991 and 2005.
items.reasoning: The 14-year recruitment window is explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Bethel Epilepsy Center, Bielefeld, Germany
items.reasoning: The specific clinical setting and location are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We excluded patients who only underwent biopsy, patients with Rasmussen's encephalitis (a progressive disease with special criteria), patients who did not have electroencephalographic video monitoring, and patients who had unclear extratemporal resections.
items.reasoning: Specific exclusion criteria are listed to ensure a homogeneous study population of resective surgery patients.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Our study includes 218 patients divided into three groups according to the time period of operation
items.reasoning: Out of 243 consecutive patients, 218 were included after logical exclusions, suggesting high participation of the eligible cohort.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The clinical characteristics of these patients, as well as detailed differences among the groups, are summarized in Table 1.
items.reasoning: Table 1 and the text provide age at onset, age at surgery, duration of epilepsy, seizure types, and pathology.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports very low attrition (4.5% missing data at 2 years) and accounts for deaths. The follow-up duration is sufficient for the outcome (prognosis after surgery).

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: In 10 patients (4.5%), the data were missing after 2 years' follow-up. Another five patients (2.25%) died
items.reasoning: Over 95% of the sample was available for the primary 2-year outcome analysis.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Research data in this study were drawn from four main sources: the patient's medical records, the postoperative routine follow-up program, additional outpatient appointments, and telephone and mail questionnaires.
items.reasoning: While multiple methods were used to capture data, specific attempts to re-engage the 10 missing patients are not detailed.

items.evidence_snippet: In 10 patients (4.5%), the data were missing after 2 years' follow-up. Another five patients (2.25%) died: one (0.4%) died in status epilepticus, and four (1.8%) died as a result of other medical causes.
items.reasoning: Reasons for death are provided, but the specific reasons for the 10 missing patients are not listed.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors like MRI findings and pathology were assessed using standardized protocols and expert review. The use of a 1.5-T MRI scanner and visual re-evaluation by a multidisciplinary team limits measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Outcome in relation to preoperative MRI pathological findings was correlated with well-circumscribed lesions (neoplastic, vascular, and cystic lesions) or less-well-circumscribed lesions (cortical dysplasia, malformation of cortical development, and gliosis) based on the MRI shape of the lesions.
items.reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (MRI lesion type) is clearly categorized.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: preoperative MRI was reevaluated visually in the case conference by two epileptologists and an epilepsy neurosurgeon to determine whether the appearance of a lesion was well circumscribed or less well circumscribed.
items.reasoning: The use of a consensus panel of experts increases the reliability of the PF measurement.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Duration of epilepsy (yr) 5 (n 37) (reference) 5 (n 181)
items.reasoning: The study uses a 5-year cut-off for duration of epilepsy, but it is not explicitly stated if this was pre-specified or data-driven.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Until 1998, a 1-T MRI scanner was used, and later a 1.5-T MRI scanner was available.
items.reasoning: The technology changed over the 15-year period, which could introduce minor measurement bias across cohorts.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: In our analysis, there were pathological findings in the resected specimen in 209 cases (95.9%), and no pathological findings in 9 cases (4.1%).
items.reasoning: Pathology and MRI data appear to be available for the entire analyzed cohort.

risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses the Engel classification, which is the gold standard for epilepsy surgery outcomes. Follow-up was systematic, involving clinical visits and standardized questionnaires.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Seizure outcome was classified by using the modified seizure classification of Engel. Engel Class I patients were seizure-free; or they had only nondisabling, simple, partial seizures...
items.reasoning: The Engel classification is a well-defined and standard outcome measure in this field.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome

items.evidence_snippet: Research data in this study were drawn from four main sources: the patient's medical records, the postoperative routine follow-up program, additional outpatient appointments, and telephone and mail questionnaires.
items.reasoning: Multiple sources of data collection, including clinical evaluation and questionnaires, support the validity of the outcome measurement.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Postoperative inpatient evaluation routinely included MRI and electroencephalography after 6 months and 2 years.
items.reasoning: A standardized follow-up protocol was applied to all patients.
